query: For high-entropy nanoalloys in high-temperature applications, what governs structural and chemical stability, and why? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, propose a controlled comparison that would distinguish it from alternatives, predict observations relative to a baseline, define the boundaries of the prediction, identify supporting evidence from the background, and state a falsifying outcome.

generation.hypothesis: For equiatomic fcc high-entropy nanoalloys, the dominant control on high-temperature structural and chemical stability is the magnitude of local lattice distortion (quantified by the atomic-size-mismatch parameter δ); a larger δ reduces bulk and surface atomic mobility (‘sluggish diffusion’) and therefore suppresses both particle coarsening and surface/chemical segregation during annealing.
generation.material_initial_state: 5 ± 1 nm CoCrFeNi fcc nanoparticles produced by inert-gas condensation, composition homogeneous to ±0.5 at %, no intentional impurities.
generation.intervention: Increase atomic-size mismatch by adding 2 at % W to form CoCrFeNiW0.1 (δ expected to rise from ≈4 % to ≈7 %). All other processing identical.
generation.conditions: Isothermal anneal at 900 °C (≈0.7 Tm of CoCrFeNi) for 24 h under high-purity Ar to suppress oxidation.
generation.structural_mediator: Average lattice distortion parameter δ (root-mean-square deviation of atomic radii from the mean).
generation.mechanism: Greater lattice distortion raises the activation energy for vacancy formation and hopping and frustrates collective atom rearrangements. This sluggish diffusion slows both (i) Ostwald ripening/coalescence of nanoparticles and (ii) thermally driven surface or grain-boundary segregation that would otherwise produce Cr- or Ni-rich shells, thereby maintaining a single-phase solid solution.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi, the W-doped nanoalloy will (a) show ≥50 % lower average grain-growth/coarsening rate constant, (b) retain near-equiatomic composition radially with <2 at % deviation across the particle after anneal, and (c) exhibit ≥30 % lower tracer self-diffusion coefficients for Fe or Ni at 900 °C.
generation.baseline: Undoped 5 nm CoCrFeNi nanoparticles processed and annealed identically.
generation.boundary: Prediction holds for particles ≤20 nm, fcc solid-solution structure, annealing temperatures between 0.6–0.8 Tm, inert atmosphere; breakdown expected if δ becomes so large that secondary intermetallic phases nucleate or if significant oxidation occurs.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of diffusion slowdown may depend on exact W distribution and possible short-range ordering; oxidation or contamination could mask effects. No direct prior data on CoCrFeNiW nanoparticles available.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two nanoalloy batches (CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNiW0.1); anneal both at 900 °C for 24 h in identical Ar-filled quartz tubes. Characterize before and after anneal.
measurements: Nanoparticle size distributions by TEM to extract coarsening rate constants
Radial composition profiles by atom probe tomography or X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling
Self-diffusion coefficients via tracer diffusion (e.g., 57Co or 59Fe) using secondary-ion mass spectrometry
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the W-doped sample shows (i) ≤10 % reduction in coarsening rate constant OR (ii) >5 at % surface enrichment/depletion of any principal element compared with the core OR (iii) ≤10 % reduction in tracer diffusion coefficient relative to baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
